title: Circuit Overlap Between Related Tasks: How Much Do the IOI and Greater-Than Circuits Share?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: high circuit overlap implies general-purpose computational primitives, making it feasible to monitor a small number of circuits for broad behavioral coverage. This directly enables practical safety monitoring. Each link is defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running circuit discovery (attribution patching) on three separate tasks, computing Jaccard similarity of edge/node sets, and ablation experiments on shared edges. Managing three circuit discovery runs and cross-task comparison requires strong familiarity with TransformerLens. Advanced for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: 3 tasks, pairwise Jaccard similarity, shared-edge ablation. The deliverable is a clear comparison matrix. Though three circuit runs are needed, each is well-documented individually.

novelty.reasoning: Merullo et al., 'Circuit Component Reuse Across Tasks in Transformer Language Models' (ICLR 2024) directly studies circuit overlap in GPT-2, finding ~78% overlap in attention heads between IOI and Colored Objects circuits. While the proposed study specifically compares IOI with Greater-Than (rather than Colored Objects), the methodology and core question of cross-task circuit overlap in GPT-2 is thoroughly addressed. The Greater-Than circuit has also been independently studied (Hanna et al.). The proposed work would be an incremental extension to a different task pair.
